## Summary — 2026-09-02 session

**What I checked first:** account equity (~$97,624), all open positions, and open orders — as required before touching anything.

**What I found:**
- 4 calendar spreads already open: **AVGO, DELL, HPE, PANW** — each short the front-month ATM call / long the back-month ATM call. That's 8 individual option legs.
- 1 stale resting order: an **NTAP** calendar (9 contracts, front 09/18 back 10/16) sitting at **strike 185**, net debit limit $3.05. NTAP's spot has since drifted to $188.82, making **190** the correct ATM strike per today's scan — the resting order was quoting a strike that's no longer representative.

**Roll analysis on the 4 existing positions:**
All four front legs expire 2026-09-04 — exactly at the 2-day "must roll" threshold in the risk rules. I pulled live IV on each front vs back leg to see if the alternate trigger (crush already captured) had also fired:
- AVGO front IV 1.37 vs scan's 1.40 → basically unchanged, no crush yet.
- DELL front IV 0.84 vs scan's 0.83 → unchanged; the big option-price swings were from the stock drifting away from strike, not IV collapsing.
- HPE front IV 1.88 vs scan's 1.87 → unchanged.
- PANW front IV read is noisy (deep OTM now, delta 0.03) — not a clean crush signal either.

So none had genuinely captured the crush — this would have been a pure **time-based** roll (close front, sell new front at the next expiry, same strike, same back leg), which in all 4 cases priced out to a net **credit** (roughly +$400 AVGO, +$565 DELL, +$216 HPE, +$234 PANW at the quotes checked), with acceptable liquidity on both legs (OI well above 10, spreads tight-to-moderate).

**What actually happened when I tried to act:**
Every one of the 8 roll-leg orders (both the closing buy-to-close legs and the new sell-to-open legs) was rejected by a hard account-level guard: *"Position cap (8) reached — code-level guard, not a suggestion."* The account is already carrying 8 option positions (legs), and the system blocks **any** new order — including closes — once that cap is hit. I did not attempt to route around this (e.g., via close_position or other paths); the message was explicit that this is a hard stop, not something to negotiate with.

I did successfully **cancel the stale NTAP order** (that's a cancellation, not a new position, so it went through), but I could not submit its corrected-strike (190) replacement, since that too would be a new order against a full cap.

**What I did NOT do, and why:**
- Did not open any of the fresh Tier A candidates (MDT, MDB, SNOW, CIEN, LULU, ZS, DOCU, IOT) — there was no capacity regardless of how attractive their term-structure ratios looked (several — SNOW 3.1x, ZS 2.9x, DOCU 2.8x — were well above threshold and would otherwise have warranted a closer look in the next batch).
- No Tier B tickers were in today's candidate list, so nothing to flag there.

**Net result today:** no new orders filled, one stale order cancelled. The four existing calendars remain open, unrolled, with their front legs now 2 days from expiry. That's a real risk sitting on the book: if the position cap doesn't free up (e.g., via the front legs simply expiring on 9/4, or a manual close in a separate session) before Friday, those shorts will run into their own expiration without the intended roll. This needs to be the first thing checked next session — either the fronts will have expired/settled (freeing capacity for a fresh roll or new entries), or a deliberate decision is needed to close a full spread to make room.
